s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic papular eruption of the extremities with a chronic time course
salient_findings: Rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on the extremities
Erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
3-month history of symptoms
No remarkable medical or family history
No concurrent medications
Previous treatment with topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets had no effect
Palms, soles, and oral mucosa not involved
Normal laboratory tests, including blood, liver and kidney function, antistreptolysin O, C-reactive protein, antinuclear antibody, and rheumatoid factor
Skin biopsy showed mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

shortlist.label: Grover disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of pruritic papules and histopathological findings of parakeratosis and vacuolar degeneration

shortlist.label: Darier disease
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by keratotic papules and histopathological features of suprabasal acantholytic dyskeratosis, which aligns with some of the patient's skin biopsy results

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with keratotic papules and can have a chronic course, although the absence of palm and sole involvement is less typical

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with pruritic, flat-topped papules and has histopathological features that include basal cell degeneration and a band-like infiltrate, which partially matches the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Keratosis follicularis
shortlist.why_kept: Involves the follicles and can present with keratotic papules, although it is less common and the clinical presentation must be carefully considered

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including intensively pruritic papules and the histopathology findings of mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and individual cell dyskeratosis, are consistent with Grover disease, a rare skin condition characterized by these features.

rejected.label: Darier disease
rejected.why: While Darier disease also presents with keratotic papules, it typically has a familial component and more pronounced dyskeratosis, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: Pityriasis rubra pilaris often involves the palms and soles, which are spared in this patient, and typically has a more widespread and progressive course.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: Lichen planus usually presents with flat-topped, violaceous papules and often involves the oral mucosa, which is not involved in this case.

rejected.label: Keratosis follicularis
rejected.why: Keratosis follicularis, also known as Darier-White disease, has a strong familial component and more pronounced follicular involvement, which is not described in the vignette.
